summary:
TWO CHECKS BUILT, ONE OF THEM RED ON SIX REAL DEFECTS, AND THE THREE CHECKS THE BRIEF OFFERED AS CANDIDATES WERE REFUSED FOR A MEASURED REASON RATHER THAN WRITTEN.

ITEM 1. The brief's first three candidates -- every domain has its default inside it, the two ends are ordered, an int lever's ends are ints -- are ALREADY REFUSED AT DECLARATION by src/spine/lever.py::_domain_ends, and I planted all EIGHT shapes it refuses at the constructor plus four controls: 8 LeverError, 4 built. I then planted the out-of-domain default in a scratch copy of src/opt/levers.py (lr_decay, default 1.0, given domain=(0.0, 0.5)) and `import spine.assemble` raised. A tree carrying one of the eight DOES NOT IMPORT, so a static restatement in tests/ could only ever fire on a tree test_census.py and test_assemble.py cannot load -- guard 61 of this repository's 60. Not written, and the ruling is recorded in docs/04_CONTRACT.md 0.5.

WHAT I WROTE INSTEAD IS THE ONE THE BRIEF CALLED MOST VALUABLE. O15 reads the hand-written refusals out of the package bodies by AST and compares their intervals with the declared pairs in both directions: PRE-EMPTION (the domain refuses everything a read-site clause refuses, so that clause can never run again) and OVER-REFUSAL (the domain is narrower than a refusal that pins both ends, so a configuration the shipped body accepts stops building). It is RED with SIX findings in FOUR packages -- OPT_LR_DECAY, OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP twice, SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC, TOK_DROPOUT, FAB_DISCOVER -- and I did not narrow it to make it green. EVERY ONE WAS DRIVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, one fresh process per cell: with the pair in place the declaration raises ('OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP=1.5 is outside its declared domain [0.0, 1.0] -- BOTH ENDS INCLUSIVE'), and with the pair neutralised the body raises the sentence that carries the MEASUREMENT ('is above 1.0, which INVERTS the mechanism...'). The two verdicts the check does NOT make were driven too: LM_DROPOUT=1.0 and OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC=1.0 both resolve and are then refused BY NAME by their bodies, which is the shape spine/lever.py prescribes, and O15 stays silent on both. O14 is the second check and is O2's rule one field over: a domain endpoint must be a literal, because _domain_ends isinstance-tests the VALUE and accepts domain=(0.0, _CEILING) and, measured, domain=(0.0, float(FABLevers.slots.default)) -- a range endpoint read out of another package's declaration with no wire and nothing in affects().

CALIBRATION, AND THE HONEST ANSWER IS THAT HISTORY CANNOT CALIBRATE THE VERDICT. I extracted all 77 commits carrying src/ and ran the extractor over every one: 31 distinct refusal sites, 0 to 44 per tree, and I OPENED ALL 31 against the first line of the refusal message each sits over. All 31 pair with the lever their own message names and every extracted interval matches the interval the message states -- zero mis-extractions. But `domain=` appears in NONE of the 77 trees, so both verdict arms had population 0 and 0 findings at every archived commit: that is not a low false-alarm rate, it is history having nothing to say, and I say so in the file rather than printing 0/0/77 as a result. What stands in for it is the live drive (8 verdicts, every one confirmed both ways) and 20 planted cases. THE RAISE REQUIREMENT IS WHAT MAKES THE EXTRACTOR SOUND: without it the recogniser matched ten GATE ARMS (`elif every > 0:`, `elif damp >= 1.0:`, `if clip > 0.0:`, `elif float(cap.lift) < 0:`) which test a lever against a literal and name it in the body and are REPORTS.

EVERY MECHANISM IS SEEN TO FAIL, which is the claim k_k16.json caught K16 making falsely. I deleted thirteen mechanisms one at a time: on the first pass FOUR were pinned by NOTHING and the whole self-test stayed green -- the raise requirement, the kill-on-rebind, the bool rejection and the table's holder-reaches-a-raise test -- and three more (the env-name pairing, the mislabelled-table abstention, the ambiguous-owned_by abstention) were unpinned after that. Seven cases were written for them and the sweep now goes RED on all 13.

ITEM 2. A LEVER GAINING A DOMAIN CHANGES NO CENSUS ROW, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. A census row has exactly nine fields on all 331 rows and not one is a range, bound, interval, minimum or maximum; the checks read five of the nine plus DEPARTURES, and `unit`, `purpose`, `reason`, `old_default` and `couples_with` are read by no check in the file. All 33 domain-carrying levers join to a census row, 0 unaccounted. docs/04_LEVERS.md DOES NOT EXIST -- it is the PLANNED consumer four files name -- so nothing is stale. I FIXED THE DRIFTED `where`: misc/WRONG_SWEEP's :463-475 now reads :517-529, and census is 8 checks + the self-test, 0 failing, from 2 failing. AND I REFUSED THE CHECK A READER WILL WANT: five of the 33 carry census unit `fraction 0..1` and domain (0.0, 2.0) because they are cosine distances on [0, 2]; a unit-vs-domain check's first finding would be a true reading called wrong, and 'fixing' either side overturns three standing rulings or refuses a 1.24 this tree measured.

ITEM 3. docs/04_CONTRACT.md gains 0.5 -- what `domain=` is, the two constants, that BOTH ARE SWITCHABLE BY CODE EDIT ONLY (no SPINE_REFUSE_* name, no census row, an operator holding only a shell cannot reach either), what turning each off costs, the floor-and-domain complementarity measured with the floor both ON and OFF in one process, and WHAT NEITHER BUYS with the OPT_LR ladder pasted: 1e6 is twenty-four orders of magnitude below the first non-finite row and still leaves every parameter at -3928. I drove the five 'inside the pair and known wrong' settings and all five build. TWO NOW-FALSE CLAIMS IN THAT DOCUMENT ARE REPAIRED and one drifted bare line number is re-cited by symbol. The quoted sentence from src/lm/api.py::resolve is left VERBATIM so O13 keeps resolving it, and the prose around it now says which half is false -- with the correction that its conclusion is true of only TWO of that function's nine refusals, not all of them, because five of the others ARE expressible as pairs and simply do not carry one.

unfinished.title: THE SIX O15 FINDINGS: a by-name refusal in four packages that the declaration now reaches first. EXACT REPAIRS, TEXT-ANCHORED.
unfinished.reason: src/opt/api.py, src/sig/api.py, src/tok/api.py, src/fabric/api.py and the levers.py files beside them are owned by other agents. I own the CHECK, not the code it reports on, and I did not weaken the check to hide them.
unfinished.detail:
EACH HAS TWO LEGAL REPAIRS AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS RIGHT PER LEVER. (A) retire the read-site clause and carry its MEASUREMENT into the lever's declaration comment, keeping the pair; or (B) delete the `domain=` and leave the ruling where it was argued. (A) is recommended everywhere except FAB_DISCOVER. There is no third option that keeps both: a clause that can never run is an untrippable guard, and its sentence -- which is the only place the measurement lives -- becomes prose nothing can print. OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP already shows what that costs: its message is BOTH unreachable AND false (see below).

(1) src/opt/api.py -- OPT_LR_DECAY, at :849 today. FIND the whole statement:
    `    if not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0:\n        raise ValueError(f"OPT_LR_DECAY={decay!r} is outside [0.0, 1.0]. 0.0 restores the "`
    ... through `..."are not.")`. The domain (0.0, 1.0) on src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers.lr_decay transcribes it EXACTLY, so the clause is dead. Retire it, and move its sentence -- '0.0 restores the pre-2026-08-26 behaviour (restarts return to full peak) and 1.0 is the full envelope; the values between are meaningful and the ones outside are not' -- into the comment under the lr_decay declaration, where it is the argument FOR the pair.

(2) src/opt/api.py -- OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP, TWO clauses, at :830 and :837 today. FIND `    if damp > 1.0:` and `    if damp < 0.0:` and their raises. domain=(0.0, 1.0) covers both. AND THE :830 MESSAGE IS FALSE AS WELL AS UNREACHABLE, which d_pop_rest.json found independently: it says a value above 1.0 'AMPLIFIES every failed restart', and src/opt/api.py::maybe_step guards its one `st.restart_amp *= ...` with `float(opt.lr_restart_damp) < 1.0`, so above 1.0 the loop goes INERT. Do not carry that sentence to the declaration; carry the true one. Its last clause, 'a Lever has no range facility', is also on d_lever.json's list of thirteen now-false prose sites.

(3) src/sig/api.py -- SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC, at :1108 today. FIND `    if frac < 0.0:` inside src/sig/api.py::warm_up and its raise. domain=(0.0, 1.0) on src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.warmup_min_frac covers it. The message is worth keeping and worth moving whole: 'A negative fraction makes a negative floor, which is not a weaker guard but NO guard'. NOTE the comment immediately under that `if` also asserts 'spine/lever.py::Lever carries `choices` and no numeric range, so units.FRACTION on the declaration is a LABEL and not a constraint' -- the first half is now false and the second half is still true and must survive the edit.

(4) src/tok/api.py -- TOK_DROPOUT, at :498 today. FIND `    if not 0.0 <= _drop <= 1.0:` and its LeverError. domain=(0.0, 1.0) transcribes it exactly. The message carries the richest measurement in the four (vocabulary 399, tok.build_mint 143, bytes_per_token 1.0, tok.dropout_skip 3999 of 4000, two successive regularized calls returning the IDENTICAL segmentation) and that must land in the declaration comment. SAME FILE, SEPARATELY: the block above it ends 'A declared per-lever domain is the general answer and is open' -- it is no longer open for this lever, and the identical sentence is in src/fabric/api.py::build and src/data/api.py::data_plan.

(5) src/fabric/api.py -- FAB_DISCOVER, at :696 today, AND THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT: the clause `_off = [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in _gated_off if v < 0.0]` refuses EIGHT levers and only FAB_DISCOVER has a pair, so retiring the clause would remove the refusal from the other seven. The repair is to remove ONE ENTRY. FIND, in the `_gated_off` tuple:
    `("FAB_DISCOVER", float(fab.discover)), ` 
and delete it, re-wrapping the tuple, with a line in the block above saying that src/fabric/levers.py::FABLevers.discover now carries domain=(0.0, 2.0) and refuses the negative at the first read. CONSEQUENCES, both of which must move in the same commit: the refusal's own prose says 'eleven' and 'these eight are guarded at `> 0.0`' and both counts drop by one; and tests/test_fabric.py::check_f4_negative_magnitude_levers_refused is titled 'eleven negative magnitude levers' and is already RED for this reason, with a verified patch in .rework/audits/d_pop_fabric.json. THE ALTERNATIVE, if the owner would rather keep eleven in one list: delete domain= from discover and leave the ruling in the body. Both are legal; leaving both standing is not.

VERIFY AFTER ANY OF THESE: `python3 tests/test_ownership.py 2>&1 | grep -A8 O15` -- the finding for that site disappears and the detail line's 'site(s) examined for pre-emption' drops by one.

unfinished.title: O15's two blind spots, named so the next reader does not take the check for more than it is
unfinished.reason: Not defects to fix; the boundary of what was built, recorded where the next agent will look.
unfinished.detail: (1) 51 refusal sites are ABSTAINED on and the detail line prints the number: 49 are an `if` whose test names a lever and is not a comparison of that lever against numeric literals -- `if _nonfinite:`, `if seg_min < 1 or seg_max < seg_min:`, `if REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD and every < 0:`, `if capacity != owners * quota:` -- and 2 are a table entry whose comprehension condition could not be read. All are skipped and counted. Abstaining can only make O15 report LESS, EXCEPT on the over-refusal arm, where an unread clause could narrow what the body accepts -- which is why that arm SETS ASIDE any lever with an abstained test, and 3 of its 5 are set aside today (OPT_LR_DECAY, OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC and TOK_DROPOUT, each because of their package's `if _nonfinite:` sweep). A grammar that read `if REFUSE_X and <cmp>:` as <cmp> whenever REFUSE_X is a module constant set True would recover three more sites and is the obvious next widening; it needs its own calibration because it reads a module-level value as a constant. (2) O15 says nothing about whether a domain is RIGHT. The direction that matters most is not written down anywhere in the tree and no static check can reach it: a domain that ADMITS a value the mechanism destroys. FAB_ALPHA=1e26 is inside every rule in tests/test_ownership.py and leaves 15 of 23 gradients non-finite.
